options.text: Creates an app from the root component and renders it into the #app element

questions.explanation: createApp builds an application instance from the root component, and .mount('#app') attaches and renders it onto the matching DOM element.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct way to bind an element's href to a `url` variable?
questions.explanation: Mustaches don't work in attributes. Use v-bind, whose shorthand is a colon: :href="url".

options.text: Whenever the HTML comes from users or untrusted sources (XSS risk)
Only when the page is in dark mode

questions.explanation: v-html renders a raw HTML string, so untrusted content can inject scripts (cross-site scripting). Use it only with trusted, sanitized HTML.

questions.prompt: A template attribute that starts with `v-` and applies reactive behavior is called a ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Directives (v-bind, v-on, v-if, v-for, v-model, …) are special v-prefixed attributes that apply reactive behavior to the DOM.

questions.prompt: Which statements about template bindings are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: {{ }} inserts a value as plain text
A binding can contain a full if-statement
Binding a value of null or undefined removes the attribute

questions.explanation: Interpolation renders text, @ is the v-on shorthand, and null/undefined removes a bound attribute. Bindings accept a single expression, not a statement like an if.

questions.prompt: In `v-on:click.prevent="onSubmit"`, match each part to what it is.
questions.explanation: A directive has a name (v-on), an optional argument after the colon (click), optional modifiers after dots (prevent), and a value expression (onSubmit).
